messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hiring Managers
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Updated level grid + geo-band benchmarking for Q3 offers (approval request)

Team —

I ran a quick market refresh for Q3 hiring (US / EU / APAC) and updated the leveling grid to better align our offer anchors with recent benchmarks. The attached CompGrid_Q3_2026_v2.xlsx includes:

- New med/90 anchors by level (L3-L6) split by primary geo cluster (US / EU / APAC).
- Recommended delta bands for outbound offers (+/- 10% standard, +/ - 15% for high-priority hires).
- A suggested approach for variable (bonus) caps in regions with different practices.

Ask: sign-off on the grid so TA can proceed with offers to the BrightCap candidate pool this week. Specifically:
1) Approve the proposed anchors for L4 and L5 in the US and APAC clusters.
2) Confirm we route any offers above the 90th percentile (per the attached) to exec approval.
3) Quick confirmation on whether Finance is comfortable with the projected incremental headcount spend for Q3 (sheet "Budget Impact").

Notes: the MarketBenchmarks_APAC-EU-US.pdf summarizes sources (Paysa, Mercer samples, and recent comp data from three peer startups). We used a 6-month blended sample to smooth short-term volatility.

If I don’t hear back by EOD tomorrow I will assume the anchors are acceptable for outreach up to the 90th percentile and will route exceptions to Vivek for approval.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Head of Talent | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: CompGrid_Q3_2026_v2.xlsx, MarketBenchmarks_APAC-EU-US.pdf

Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated level grid + geo-band benchmarking for Q3 offers (approval request)

Thanks Priya — quick read-through and a couple of questions.

1) For L4/L5 in the US you moved the 50->90 anchor up ~8% vs current grid. Can you add two real example total comp lines (base + OTE/bonus if applicable) so I can see what these offers look like for an average vs top candidate?

2) For APAC you’ve got a larger spread. Is that driven by HK/SIN outliers, or is it broader across India/SEA as well? If HK/SIN are driving it, we should consider having a sub-cluster because payroll tax and equity expectations differ.

3) If the proposal increases the Q3 budget by >$250k we should route to Finance and include that in the July forecast cadence.

I’m supportive in principle but want the example lines (2–3 rows) and the headcount cost delta before final sign-off.

Vivek
Chief Operating Officer
vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

Priya — useful work, thank you. A few inline notes (also added comments in the spreadsheet):

- L4 examples: see rows added in the CompGrid worksheet (Base / Bonus / Equity 3yr). I used two data points: a typical hire and a top-of-band hire for a high-priority role.
- APAC: you are right, HK/SIN are skewing the cluster. Recommend splitting APAC into APAC-High (HK/SIN) and APAC-Mid (IN/SEA) so offers don’t unintentionally inflate India offers.
- EU variable cap: our legal/ben team flagged that certain countries require different bonus structures. Please cap variable comp at 10% for the EU anchors; we can top up equity instead.

A couple of practical asks:
- Add a short footnote in the spreadsheet that explains routing thresholds (who approves what).
- Can we get a one-page summary for the hiring managers so TA can use it as a playbook?

If Finance gives a greenlight on the budget impact I’m happy to push rollout to Hiring Managers by Wednesday.

Best —
Laura Bennett
VP, People Ops
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Folks —

Reviewed the CompGrid_Q3_2026_v2 and Budget Impact tab. High level: I can approve moving forward with the proposed anchors for the US and APAC-Mid clusters as long as the following controls are added:

- Any single-offer total comp that exceeds the proposed 90th percentile by > 15% must be routed for Exec sign-off (Vivek or CFO).
- Cumulative incremental spend above the baseline forecast for Q3 (sheet shows ~$210k) must be approved by Finance (Aditya/FP&A). Threshold to trigger formal routing: $250k.
- For EU hires follow Laura’s guidance: cap variable comp at 10% and use equity top-ups where needed.

I will clear spend up to $225k against the current recruiting bucket today; anything beyond that requires us to move amounts from contingency or delay some non-critical searches.

Please confirm that the TA team will implement the routing matrix and a one-pager for managers before offers go out. Also please add Offer_Approval_Routing_Playbook.pdf to the Drive link so recruiting has a single source of truth.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

- Routing: exceptions (offers >90th + >15% over anchor) will go to Exec (Vivek/CFO). TA will tag those in Workday and include "ExecRouting" in the HubSpot deal notes.
